rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for evaluating or judging the quality or value of something.

example.english: I would rate this restaurant's service.
example.traditional: 我會評價呢間餐廳嘅服務。
example.jyutping: ngo5 wui5 ping4 gaa3 ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 ge3 fuk6 mou6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for physical speed or the speed at which something changes or progresses.

example.english: This machine has a very fast operating rate.
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 gei1 ge3 cuk1 dou6 hou2 faai3

rows.note: Use this when saying that something deserves attention or is worth doing or mentioning.

example.english: I’d rate this movie as worth watching.
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zik6 dak1 jat1 tai2

rows.note: Use this when rate means the amount charged for a thing or service, especially a set service charge.

example.english: What is the rate at this laundromat?
example.traditional: 呢間洗衣舖嘅收費幾多錢呀？
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 sai2 ji1 pou3 ge3 sau1 fai3 gei2 do1 cin2 aa3

rows.note: Use this for the proportional relationship between two amounts or values.

example.english: The rate of oil to water is one to three.
example.traditional: 油同水嘅比例係一比三。
example.jyutping: jau4 tung4 seoi2 ge3 bei2 lai6 hai6 jat1 bei2 saam1

rows.note: Use this specifically for pay calculated for each hour worked.

example.english: What is the minimum hourly rate now?
example.traditional: 而家最低時薪係幾多呀？
example.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 zeoi3 dai1 si4 san1 hai6 gei2 do1 aa3

rows.note: Use this for placing someone or something in an ordinal or competitive ranking.

example.english: They rate third in the league right now.
example.jyutping: ni1 deoi6 bo1 ji4 gaa1 paai4 ming4 dai6 saam1

rows.note: Use this when “rate” means to like or approve of something rather than assess it formally.

example.jyutping: ngo5 gei2 zung1 ji3 ni1 sau2 go1
